verses.commentary: Israel was a spreading vine. Flourishing, productive. He brought forth fruit for himself. Self-serving growth. As his fruit increased, he built more altars. Prosperity funded idolatry. As his land prospered, he adorned his sacred stones. Wealth decorated false worship.

Their heart is deceitful. Divided loyalty. Now they must bear their guilt. Consequences arrive. The Lord will demolish their altars. What they built, God destroys. Destroy their sacred stones. No religious artifact survives.

Then they will say: We have no king. Political collapse. Because we did not revere the Lord. The connection drawn. But even if we had a king, what could he do? Helpless recognition. Leadership cannot save.
They make many promises. Empty words. Take false oaths. Broken commitments. Make agreements. Then break them. Lawsuits spring up like poisonous weeds. Litigation everywhere, toxic growth.

The people of Samaria fear for the calf-idol of Beth-aven. They worry about their god. Its people will mourn over it. The worshipers grieve. Its priests who rejoiced in its splendor. The religious professionals mourn. Because it is taken into exile. The god goes captive.

It will be carried to Assyria as tribute for the great king. Their god becomes a tax payment. Ephraim will be disgraced. Shame from their choices. Israel ashamed of its foreign alliances. The allies become humiliation.
Samaria's king will be destroyed. Royal power swept away. Like a twig on the surface of the waters. Insignificant, carried off.

The high places of wickedness will be destroyed. The sin of Israel. Thorns and thistles cover their altars. Weeds reclaim sacred sites. They will say to the mountains: Cover us! And to the hills: Fall on us! Jesus quotes this of Jerusalem's destruction (Luke 23:30). Revelation 6:16 echoes it for final judgment.
Since the days of Gibeah you have sinned. Ancient pattern. And there you have remained. No progress from wickedness. Will not war overtake the evildoers in Gibeah? The old judgment returns.
When I please, I will punish them. Divine timing. Nations gathered against them. Coalition of judgment. To put them in bonds for their double sin. Double punishment for covenant people.

Ephraim is a trained heifer that loves to thresh. Easy work, eating while walking. So I will put a yoke on her fair neck. Harder labor coming. I will drive Ephraim. No more freedom. Judah must plow, Jacob break ground. All must work.

Sow righteousness for yourselves. The agricultural command. Reap the fruit of unfailing love. The harvest of right living. Break up your unplowed ground. New cultivation needed. It is time to seek the Lord. The moment for return. Until he comes and showers his righteousness on you. God's response to seeking.

But you have planted wickedness. The wrong seed. You have reaped evil. The wrong harvest. You have eaten the fruit of deception. The wrong meal. Because you depended on your own strength. Self-reliance as root sin. And on your many warriors. Military trust misplaced.

The roar of battle will rise against your people. War comes. All your fortresses devastated. What protected will fall. As Shalman devastated Beth Arbel. An otherwise unknown atrocity. Mothers dashed to the ground with their children. War's horror.

So it will happen to you, Bethel. The judgment arrives. Because your wickedness is great. The reason clear. When that day dawns, the king of Israel will be completely destroyed. Total end of monarchy.
